programs.summary: One- and three-week summer courses for academically advanced students, from enrichment to honors and college-level courses. Offered online and in person at Northwestern and other Chicago-area sites.

programs.title: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
programs.summary: Live online summer courses in small classes for academically strong students in grades 8 to 11, in subjects including math, physics, computer science, biology and engineering.
body: Who can apply: Grades 8 to 11.

programs.title: Summer@Brown
programs.summary: Non-credit courses at the level of first-year college classes, one to five weeks long, across more than 300 subjects including many STEM and engineering courses. Students live on campus or commute.
body: Who can apply: Completed 9th grade.

programs.title: Yale Young Global Scholars: Innovations in Science and Technology
programs.summary: A two-week summer session at Yale with faculty lectures, small seminars and a group capstone. In the science and technology track, students research a global problem and propose a solution.

programs.title: UChicago Summer Immersion
programs.summary: Three-week residential courses at UChicago taught at the undergraduate level. STEM courses have included biotechnology, infectious disease and astrophysics.
body: Who can apply: Grades 9 to 11, at least 14 years old.

programs.title: Penn Summer Academies
programs.org: University of Pennsylvania School of Arts and Sciences
programs.summary: Two- and three-week non-credit summer academies at Penn in one subject, such as mathematics, chemistry, experimental physics, neuroscience, biomedical research or coding.

programs.title: Harvard Summer School Secondary School Program
programs.summary: High school students take Harvard college courses for credit alongside college students, in four- or seven-week sessions on campus or online. Options include math, science and computer science courses.
body: Who can apply: At least 16, graduating high school 2027 to 2029.

programs.title: Boston University Summer High School Programs
programs.summary: Several summer programs for high school students at BU, from college credit courses to a research internship in science and engineering labs (RISE).

programs.title: Duke Pre-College Programs
programs.summary: Summer programs for middle and high school students at Duke, including STEM, engineering, aerospace and neuroscience options. Residential and day sessions last about two weeks.

programs.title: Columbia University Pre-College Programs
programs.org: Columbia University School of Professional Studies
programs.summary: Summer and online courses for high school students taught by Columbia instructors, with STEM options such as engineering, computer science and biomedical topics.
programs.format: Hybrid, New York, NY, and online

programs.title: Carleton Summer Liberal Arts Institute (SLAI)
programs.summary: Three-week residential programs at Carleton for high school students, including computer science and science programs. Students can earn Carleton course credit.

programs.title: Cornell Precollege Studies
programs.org: Cornell University School of Continuing Education
programs.summary: Summer courses for high school students at Cornell and online. Students take college credit courses or shorter non-credit programs, including STEM subjects.

programs.title: Rice Precollege Programs
programs.summary: Online courses for high school students ages 13 and up in STEM, medicine and other subjects, taught by Rice faculty.

programs.title: Notre Dame Pre-College Programs
programs.summary: Summer residential, online and study abroad programs for high school students at Notre Dame. STEM options include Introduction to Engineering and a physics program (QuarkNet).

programs.title: Space Camp and Advanced Space Academy
programs.summary: Week-long residential camps in Huntsville with astronaut training exercises, engineering challenges and a simulated space mission. Space Camp is for ages 9 to 11, Space Academy for 12 to 14, and Advanced Space Academy for 15 to 18. There are also aviation and robotics camps.

programs.title: NASA SEES High School Summer Intern Program
programs.org: University of Texas at Austin Center for Space Research, with NASA and Texas Space Grant Consortium
programs.summary: A summer internship that starts with remote work and ends with two weeks at UT Austin. Interns work with NASA scientists and engineers on Earth and space science projects, analyzing real data.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, current sophomores or juniors, at least 16 by early July.

programs.title: Civil Air Patrol National Cadet Special Activities
programs.summary: More than 50 week-long summer activities for Civil Air Patrol cadets, including flight training academies, aerospace and STEM career exploration, and emergency services training. Cadets must first join CAP, which is open from age 12.
body: Who can apply: Civil Air Patrol cadets, most activities for ages 15 to 20.

programs.title: EAA Aviation and Flight Summer Camps
programs.summary: One-week EAA Air Academy camps in Oshkosh for middle and high school students, with aviation classes and hands-on time with instructors and mentors. EAA also runs a camp for young women and free Young Eagles flights.

programs.title: Embry-Riddle Summer Camps
programs.summary: Day and overnight camps at the Daytona Beach and Prescott campuses on flight, aerospace and mechanical engineering, robotics, space and security.
programs.format: In person, Daytona Beach, FL, and Prescott, AZ

programs.title: National Flight Academy
programs.summary: Aviation-themed STEM programs for grades 6 to 12 at the National Naval Aviation Museum, where students plan and fly simulated missions using math and science.

programs.title: New Jersey Governor's School of Engineering and Technology (GSET)
programs.summary: A free four-week residential program at Rutgers for New Jersey juniors. Students take engineering courses, do a team research project and visit companies, after about 40 hours of reading before the program starts.
body: Who can apply: New Jersey high school juniors nominated by their school.
programs.when: Usually winter; decisions in early April

programs.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences (PGSS)
programs.org: Pennsylvania Governor's Schools, hosted at Carnegie Mellon University
programs.summary: A free five-week residential program at Carnegie Mellon for Pennsylvania students between junior and senior year. Students take science and math classes, do lab work and finish a team research project. About 72 students are chosen.
body: Who can apply: Pennsylvania high school juniors.
programs.when: Applications open October 2026, due in winter

programs.title: Governor's School of North Carolina
programs.org: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction
programs.summary: A four-week residential summer program on two college campuses for gifted North Carolina high school students. Students choose an area such as natural science or mathematics and take classes with no tests or grades.
body: Who can apply: North Carolina rising seniors, nominated through their school district.
programs.when: Nomination through your school, usually fall and winter
programs.cost: $600 tuition, usually paid by the nominating school
programs.format: In person, Greensboro College and Meredith College, NC

programs.title: Tennessee Governor's School for the Sciences and Engineering (GSSE)
programs.summary: A four-week residential program at UT Knoxville with common STEM courses in the morning and elective STEM courses and labs in the afternoon. Students earn college credit. Funded by the Tennessee Department of Education.
body: Who can apply: Tennessee high school students.

programs.title: Missouri Scholars Academy
programs.summary: A residential summer academy at Mizzou for academically gifted Missouri students. Scholars pick a major and a minor from a mix of subjects, including science and engineering topics such as electronics and forensic science.
body: Who can apply: Missouri rising high school juniors.
programs.when: Nomination through your school, usually winter

programs.title: Kentucky Governor's Scholars Program
programs.summary: A free five-week residential program for Kentucky students between junior and senior year, held on three college campuses. Scholars take classes in about 25 areas, including physical science, engineering, forensic science and biotechnology.
body: Who can apply: Kentucky high school juniors.
programs.format: In person, Centre College, Morehead State and Murray State, KY

programs.title: Mississippi Governor's School
programs.summary: A free two-week residential honors program at MUW for Mississippi rising juniors and seniors, with courses, leadership activities and service projects. Students earn three hours of honors college credit.
body: Who can apply: Mississippi students in 10th or 11th grade.

programs.title: Arkansas Governor's School
programs.summary: A free four-week residential program for Arkansas juniors. Students study one area, including mathematics or natural science, plus general classes.
body: Who can apply: Arkansas high school juniors.
programs.when: Nomination through your school, usually fall

programs.title: Georgia Governor's Honors Program (GHP)
programs.org: Georgia Office of Workforce and Education Success
programs.summary: A four-week residential summer program on a Georgia college campus for sophomores and juniors. Students study one major area, with options that include math, science and technology fields. Housing and meals are covered.
body: Who can apply: Georgia high school sophomores and juniors.
programs.when: Nomination through your school, usually fall

programs.title: Virginia Summer Residential Governor's School for Mathematics, Science and Technology
programs.org: Virginia Department of Education, hosted at the University of Lynchburg
programs.summary: A three-week residential program for Virginia rising juniors and seniors with classes, labs, field studies and research projects in topics like astronomy, geology, physics, programming and upper-level math. About 130 students are accepted.
body: Who can apply: Virginia rising juniors and seniors.
programs.when: Nomination through your school division, usually fall and winter

programs.title: Jefferson Lab/VIMS Summer Residential Governor's School
programs.org: William and Mary Center for Gifted Education
programs.summary: A four-week mentorship program where Virginia students do research with scientists, either in engineering and physics at Jefferson Lab or in marine science at the Virginia Institute of Marine Science.
body: Who can apply: Virginia rising juniors and seniors.
programs.when: Nomination through your school division, usually fall and winter
programs.format: In person, Newport News and Gloucester Point, VA

programs.title: Governor's Schools of West Virginia
programs.summary: Free summer residential programs on West Virginia campuses for students in grades 9 to 11. Options include the Governor's Computer Science Institute and the Governor's Honors Academy, along with arts and business schools.
body: Who can apply: West Virginia students in grades 9 to 11.

programs.title: GSSM GoSciTech Summer Camps
programs.org: South Carolina Governor's School for Science and Mathematics
programs.summary: STEM summer camps run by South Carolina's public residential science and math high school. There is a six-day residential camp with more than 20 courses, plus day camps at technical colleges and a virtual camp.
body: Who can apply: Rising grades 6 to 10.

programs.title: Governor's School of New Jersey Program in the Sciences
programs.summary: A free three-week residential program at Drew for New Jersey students who have finished junior year. Students take science and math courses, work in labs and do a research project with Drew faculty.
body: Who can apply: New Jersey high school juniors.

programs.title: North Dakota Governor's School
programs.summary: A residential summer program at NDSU for North Dakota students who have finished sophomore or junior year. Students pick a science, technology, engineering or math pathway, do projects and research, and can earn college credit.
body: Who can apply: North Dakota sophomores and juniors.

programs.title: Governor's Institutes of Vermont
programs.summary: One- and two-week residential summer institutes for Vermont high school students on topics that include engineering, mathematical sciences, technology and design, weather and climate science, and health and medicine.
body: Who can apply: Vermont students in grades 9 to 11.
programs.cost: Sliding scale tuition, as low as $10

programs.title: Wyoming Summer High School Institute (HSI)
programs.summary: A three-week residential program at UW for Wyoming juniors. Students take two college-level courses taught by UW faculty, on topics that have included genetics, energy and robotics, and do hands-on research.
body: Who can apply: Wyoming high school juniors.

programs.title: Alabama Governor's School
programs.summary: A two-week residential honors program at Samford for Alabama rising juniors and seniors. Each student takes one morning and one afternoon seminar with hands-on work, on a mix of academic subjects.
body: Who can apply: Alabama students in 10th or 11th grade.
programs.when: Nomination through your school, usually winter

programs.title: South Dakota Governor's Camp
programs.org: University of South Dakota School of Education
programs.summary: A week-long residential STEAM camp at USD for gifted and high-achieving students entering grades 6 to 9.
body: Who can apply: Students entering grades 6 to 9.

programs.title: Operation Catapult
programs.summary: A residential program of about 12 days at Rose-Hulman where students work in small teams on an engineering or science project and present it at the end.
body: Who can apply: Students finishing sophomore or junior year, with a year of chemistry or physics.
programs.when: Rolling, first come first served in spring

programs.title: USNA Summer STEM
programs.summary: A week-long engineering and design camp at the Naval Academy with labs and team challenges in mechanical and electrical engineering, robotics, cybersecurity and naval architecture. Each session is for one grade level.
body: Who can apply: Rising 9th to 11th graders.

programs.title: Michigan Tech Summer Youth Programs
programs.summary: Week-long residential explorations for middle and high school students at Michigan Tech, many of them in engineering and science. Students live in the dorms and do hands-on classes.

programs.title: Smith College Summer Science and Engineering Program (SSEP)
programs.summary: A two-week residential program at Smith where students take one hands-on science or engineering course with lab and field work, taught by faculty with undergraduate mentors.
body: Who can apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12.

programs.title: NYU Tandon K12 STEM Summer Programs
programs.summary: A set of summer programs at NYU Tandon for middle and high school students, including cybersecurity (CS4CS), machine learning, robotics, game design and smart cities. ARISE is a longer research program in NYU labs.

programs.title: Vanderbilt Summer Academy
programs.org: Vanderbilt University Programs for Talented Youth
programs.summary: One-week residential courses at Vanderbilt for academically advanced students in grades 7 to 12. Students take one accelerated course, with options that include science topics like nanotechnology.
body: Who can apply: Grades 7 to 12, with qualifying test scores or other evidence.

programs.title: WPI Frontiers
programs.summary: A residential summer program at WPI where students take a STEM or business major with a humanities, arts or business minor. Classes include lectures, projects and labs.
body: Who can apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders.
programs.when: Rolling; aid deadline March 15, final April 30

programs.title: Cooper Union Summer STEM
programs.org: The Cooper Union Albert Nerken School of Engineering
programs.summary: Three- and six-week day classes at Cooper Union where high school students work on college-level design and engineering projects, some tied to faculty research.
body: Who can apply: Students who have completed grades 9 to 11.

programs.title: MIT PRIMES
programs.summary: A year-long research program in math and bioinformatics, including applied math and theoretical computer science, with mentors from MIT. The main program is for sophomores and juniors who live in Greater Boston.
body: PRIMES-USA has the same deadlines and is for sophomores and juniors anywhere in the US, working remotely.
programs.when: Applications due in early November, program runs the calendar year
programs.format: In person, Boston area. PRIMES-USA is remote

programs.title: PRIMES Circle
programs.summary: A free spring program for Boston-area high school students, with a focus on students from groups underrepresented in math. Small groups read and present on math topics with a mentor.
body: Who can apply: Boston-area high school students.

programs.title: PRIMES STEP
programs.summary: A free program for Boston-area middle school students. Students meet weekly at MIT to learn advanced math and work on research problems as a group.
body: Who can apply: Middle school students from Greater Boston.

programs.title: Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP)
programs.summary: A year-long program where New York City high school students do research with museum scientists in fields like astrophysics, genomics and paleontology. Students who finish receive a stipend.
body: Who can apply: NYC high school students.

programs.title: The Junior Academy
programs.summary: An online program where students join international teams to work on research challenges set by companies and organizations, with help from expert mentors.
body: Who can apply: Ages 13 to 17, worldwide.

programs.title: Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP)
programs.summary: A school-year program where high school classes or clubs do a molecular biology and bioinformatics research project and publish their DNA sequences. Teachers and a few students start at a summer institute.

programs.title: Polygence Research Mentorship Program
programs.summary: An online program that pairs a student with a mentor, often a graduate student, to finish a research project, paper or product of the student's choice over several months.

programs.title: Lumiere Research Scholar Program
programs.summary: An online program where a student works one on one with a PhD mentor for 12 weeks or longer to write an independent research paper.

programs.title: Horizon Academic Research Program
programs.summary: An online program where students take a small seminar or work one on one with a professor or PhD mentor and write a research paper.

programs.title: Pioneer Research Institute
programs.summary: An online research program where a student works with a university professor, first in a small group and then one on one, to write a research paper. Students can earn college credit.

programs.title: NIH High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
programs.summary: Students spend a summer doing biomedical research in an NIH lab, mostly on the Bethesda campus. They present a poster at the end of the summer.
body: Who can apply: Age 17 or older, US citizens or permanent residents, enrolled at least half time in high school.
programs.format: In person, NIH campuses, mainly Bethesda, MD

programs.title: NIH High School Scientific Training and Enrichment Program (HiSTEP)
programs.summary: A summer program at NIH for rising seniors from schools with many low-income families. Students build lab and science skills and can return the next summer as interns.
body: Who can apply: Rising seniors from DC-area schools with a high share of students on free or reduced lunch.

programs.title: AEOP High School Apprenticeship Program (HSAP)
programs.summary: High school students work in an Army-funded research lab at a university for a summer, doing hands-on science or engineering with a mentor.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents, age 16 or older.
programs.format: In person, University labs across the US

programs.title: AEOP Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
programs.summary: High school students spend a summer as apprentices in Army research labs, working on a real project with a scientist or engineer.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, age 16 or older.
programs.format: In person, Army labs across the US

programs.title: Navy Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
programs.summary: An eight-week summer apprenticeship at a Navy lab. High school students work on a research project with a Navy scientist or engineer.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, age 16 or older, finished at least 9th grade.
programs.format: In person, Navy labs across the US

programs.title: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP)
programs.org: National Institute of Standards and Technology
programs.summary: High school students volunteer for a summer in a NIST lab and work on a research project with a staff scientist. It is unpaid.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, finished at least junior year by the start of the program.
programs.format: In person, Gaithersburg, MD and Boulder, CO

programs.title: Argonne High School Research Programs
programs.summary: Research programs at Argonne for honors and AP-level high school students, who work with lab scientists on projects.
body: Who can apply: Mainly Chicago-area high school students.
programs.when: Varies by program, check in winter

programs.title: Argonne Bridge Into Internships
programs.summary: An eight-week summer program for recent high school graduates starting STEM degrees. Students work two days a week with a lab mentor and spend the rest on professional skills.
body: Who can apply: Recent high school graduates starting college in STEM.

programs.title: Brookhaven High School Research Program (HSRP)
programs.summary: A six-week summer program where high school students work on a research project with Brookhaven scientists and engineers, then present a poster or talk.
body: Who can apply: Age 16 or older, finished 11th grade recommended, US citizens or permanent residents.

programs.title: Fermilab TARGET Program
programs.summary: A six-week summer internship for Illinois high school sophomores and juniors. Half the day is research with a Fermilab mentor and half is workshops.
body: Who can apply: Illinois high school sophomores and juniors.

programs.title: ORNL Next Generation STEM Internship Program (NGSI)
programs.summary: A 7 to 10 week summer internship at Oak Ridge for high school juniors, seniors and recent graduates, working on projects with lab staff.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents, rising juniors and seniors or recent graduates.

programs.title: Los Alamos High School Internship Program
programs.summary: Paid work at the lab for Northern New Mexico high school seniors. Students pick projects from a list and a mentor chooses who to hire.
body: Who can apply: Northern New Mexico high school students, age 16 or older, GPA 3.0 or higher.
programs.when: Varies, check the project list each year

programs.title: Jefferson Lab High School Summer Honors Program
programs.summary: A six-week paid summer internship where local high school students do a research project at Jefferson Lab and attend workshops and lectures.
body: Who can apply: Age 16 or older, attend a high school within 60 miles of the lab, GPA 3.5 or higher.

programs.title: PPPL High School Summer Internship
programs.summary: Graduating high school seniors spend the summer working full time on a project with PPPL research or engineering staff.
body: Who can apply: Graduating high school seniors, age 16 or older.

programs.title: NSA High School Work Study Program
programs.summary: High school seniors work part time at NSA during their senior year in areas like computer science, business or languages. Students need a security clearance.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, age 16 by December 31 of junior year, live within commuting distance of an NSA site.
programs.format: In person, NSA sites in MD, GA, TX, HI, CO

programs.title: CSHL Partners for the Future
programs.summary: Long Island high school juniors are nominated by their schools and do research in a CSHL lab part time from their senior year onward.
body: Who can apply: Long Island high school juniors nominated by their school.
programs.when: School nomination, usually spring of junior year
programs.format: In person, Cold Spring Harbor, NY

programs.title: MITRE High School Student Program
programs.summary: A paid eight-week summer job where high school students work as technical aides on MITRE projects in areas like AI, cybersecurity and health.
body: Who can apply: Age 14 or older, most roles need US citizenship.
programs.format: In person, Bedford, MA, McLean, VA and other MITRE sites

programs.title: JHU APL ASPIRE
programs.org: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
programs.summary: High school juniors and seniors complete a 190-hour internship with an APL staff mentor on a project in areas like aerospace, cybersecurity or biology. It is unpaid.
body: Who can apply: High school juniors and seniors living in parts of Maryland, Northern Virginia or DC.

programs.title: AMNH Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP)
programs.summary: New York City high school students spend a year doing research with a museum scientist in fields like astronomy, biology and earth science.
body: Award: $2,500 stipend on completion.
Who can apply: NYC high school students in 10th or 11th grade.

programs.title: NASA OSTEM Internships
programs.summary: Paid internships at NASA centers for high school and college students. Interns work on a project with a NASA mentor in the spring, summer or fall session.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, age 16 or older, GPA 3.0 or higher.
programs.when: Three sessions; summer applications usually close in late February
programs.format: Hybrid, NASA centers across the US, some virtual

programs.title: AEOP College Qualified Leaders (CQL)
programs.summary: College students and recent high school graduates work in Army labs with scientists and engineers. Many interns return for several summers.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, college students.
programs.format: In person, Army labs across the US

programs.title: Naval Research Enterprise Internship Program (NREIP)
programs.summary: A ten-week summer research internship at a Navy lab for college and graduate students.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, college juniors, seniors and graduate students.
programs.format: In person, Navy labs across the US

programs.title: AFRL Scholars Program
programs.org: Air Force Research Laboratory and USRA
programs.summary: Paid summer research at Air Force Research Laboratory sites. Students from high school through graduate school work on projects in areas like space, materials and directed energy.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, age 16 or older.
programs.when: Usually winter, check the site in fall
programs.format: In person, AFRL sites in several states

programs.title: SLAC Summer Internship Program
programs.summary: Paid summer jobs at SLAC for students 18 and older, from high school seniors to graduate students. Work ranges from technical support to research tasks.
body: Who can apply: Age 18 or older, authorized to work in the US.

programs.title: Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
programs.org: US Department of Energy, Office of Science
programs.summary: Paid research internships at 17 DOE national labs. Undergraduates and recent graduates work on a project with a lab scientist for a summer or a semester.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents, age 18 or older, in college or a recent graduate.
programs.when: Summer term usually closes in early January; fall and spring terms have separate deadlines
programs.cost: Paid stipend, housing and travel help

programs.title: Community College Internships (CCI)
programs.org: US Department of Energy, Office of Science
programs.summary: Paid technical internships at DOE labs for community college students, working with lab technicians and engineers on projects.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents enrolled at a community college.
programs.when: Summer term usually closes in early January

programs.title: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR)
programs.org: US Department of Energy, Office of Science
programs.summary: PhD students spend 3 to 12 months doing part of their thesis research at a DOE national lab with a lab scientist.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents in a PhD program.
programs.when: Usually two calls a year, spring and fall

programs.title: ORISE Undergraduate Internships
programs.org: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
programs.summary: ORISE runs internships for many federal agencies, including DOE, CDC, FDA, EPA and the military. Students search and apply through the Zintellect site.
body: Who can apply: Mostly US citizens, varies by opportunity.
programs.format: In person, Federal agencies and labs across the US

programs.title: Lawrence Livermore Student Internships
programs.summary: Paid summer and year-round internships at LLNL in science, engineering and computing. Students apply to posted intern jobs.
programs.when: Rolling, most summer postings open in fall and winter

programs.title: Sandia Internships and Co-ops
programs.summary: Paid internships and co-ops at Sandia in engineering, computing and science, open to high school seniors through graduate students.
body: Who can apply: Age 16 or older, GPA 3.0 or higher, most jobs need US citizenship.
programs.when: Rolling, most summer postings open in fall
programs.format: In person, Albuquerque, NM and Livermore, CA

programs.title: PNNL Internships
programs.summary: Paid internships at PNNL for high school, college and graduate students, through lab hiring and DOE programs like SULI.
programs.format: In person, Richland, WA and other PNNL sites

programs.title: National Laboratory of the Rockies Internships (formerly NREL)
programs.summary: Paid internships in applied energy research at the DOE lab in Golden, Colorado, which was called NREL until December 2025.

programs.title: Berkeley Lab Student Programs
programs.summary: Berkeley Lab's education office runs internships for high school, community college and university students, including SULI and CCI placements.

programs.title: Ames National Laboratory Student Opportunities
programs.summary: Research internships at Ames Lab and Iowa State University, including SULI, CCI and a five-week data science summer school for early undergraduates.

programs.title: NSA Student Internships
programs.summary: Paid summer internships and co-ops at NSA for college and graduate students in math, computer science, cybersecurity, engineering and languages.
body: Who can apply: US citizens who can get a security clearance.
programs.when: Usually fall, about a year ahead because of the security clearance
programs.format: In person, Fort Meade, MD and other NSA sites

programs.title: CIA Student Programs
programs.summary: Paid internships and co-ops at CIA, including technical roles in science, engineering, data and cyber. Students apply early because of the clearance process.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, age 18 or older, who can get a security clearance.
programs.when: Usually 9 to 12 months before the start date

programs.title: NIST Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF)
programs.org: National Institute of Standards and Technology
programs.summary: Undergraduates spend about 11 weeks doing research in a NIST lab with a staff scientist.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents in college.
programs.format: In person, Gaithersburg, MD and Boulder, CO

programs.title: Smithsonian Internships
programs.summary: Internships across Smithsonian museums and research centers, including science work at the Natural History museum, the Environmental Research Center, the Tropical Research Institute and the Astrophysical Observatory. Some are paid.
programs.when: Varies by unit, many summer deadlines are in winter
programs.format: Hybrid, Washington, DC area and field stations

programs.title: NOAA Ernest F. Hollings Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for sophomores that includes a paid ten-week summer internship at a NOAA site between junior and senior year.
body: Award: Up to $9,500 a year for two years of school plus the paid internship.
Who can apply: US citizens, college sophomores.
programs.format: In person, NOAA sites across the US

programs.title: NOAA EPP/MSI Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for students at minority-serving institutions that includes two paid summer internships at NOAA.
body: Who can apply: US citizens, sophomores at minority-serving institutions.
programs.format: In person, NOAA sites across the US

programs.title: DoD SMART Scholarship
programs.summary: Full tuition plus a stipend for STEM college and graduate students, with paid summer internships at a Defense lab and a job there after graduation.
body: Award: Full tuition, stipend and summer internships.
Who can apply: US citizens, age 18 or older, in college or graduate school.
programs.format: In person, Defense labs across the US

programs.title: NASA Pathways Internship Program
programs.summary: Paid federal internships at NASA that can lead to a full-time job after graduation. Students alternate school with work terms.
body: Who can apply: US citizens enrolled at least half time.
programs.when: Postings open a few times a year on USAJOBS

programs.title: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
programs.summary: College, graduate and professional students spend a summer doing biomedical research in an NIH lab and present at Summer Poster Day.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents, age 18 or older, enrolled in college.
programs.format: In person, NIH campuses, mainly Bethesda, MD

programs.title: NIH Postbaccalaureate IRTA
programs.summary: Recent college graduates work full time in an NIH lab for one or two years before graduate or medical school.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents who finished a bachelor's degree within the last three years.

programs.title: Eugene and Ruth Roberts Summer Student Academy
programs.summary: High school and college students work full time for 10 weeks on a biomedical research team at City of Hope, with weekly seminars and a final presentation.
body: Who can apply: Age 16 or older, US citizens or permanent residents, finished high school biology and chemistry.

programs.title: St. Jude Pediatric Oncology Education (POE) Program
programs.summary: A summer internship in lab or clinical research at St. Jude for college and professional students. Each student works on a faculty mentor's project and attends daily talks.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents in college, medical or other professional school.

programs.title: Fred Hutch High School Programs
programs.summary: Fred Hutch runs summer research internships for high school students in the Seattle area, where they work in a lab and learn cancer biology.
body: Who can apply: Washington state high school students.

programs.title: Fred Hutch Summer Undergraduate Research Program
programs.summary: Undergraduates spend ten weeks doing research in a Fred Hutch lab, with seminars and a closing symposium.

programs.title: Salk High School Scholars Program
programs.summary: San Diego-area high school students work in a Salk lab for eight weeks in the summer on a research project with a scientist.
body: Who can apply: San Diego County high school students, age 16 or older.

programs.title: Scripps Research High School Internships
programs.summary: San Diego-area high school students spend the summer working in a Scripps Research lab on a chemistry or biology project with a mentor.
body: Who can apply: San Diego-area high school students.

programs.title: JAX Summer Student Program
programs.summary: High school and college students spend ten weeks doing genetics research with a JAX scientist and present their work at the end.
body: Who can apply: Age 16 or older, finished junior year of high school.
programs.format: In person, Bar Harbor, ME and Farmington, CT

programs.title: CSHL Undergraduate Research Program
programs.summary: Undergraduates spend ten weeks doing research in a Cold Spring Harbor lab in areas like cancer, neuroscience, plant biology and computational biology.
programs.format: In person, Cold Spring Harbor, NY

programs.title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
programs.summary: High school juniors and seniors spend eight weeks doing medical research in a Stanford lab, grouped by institutes like cancer, immunology or neuroscience.
body: Who can apply: High school juniors and seniors, age 16 or older, US citizens or permanent residents.

programs.title: MSK Summer Student Program
programs.summary: Undergraduates join a lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering for the summer to do cancer research. MSK also runs a summer program in biostatistics.

programs.title: AEOP Undergraduate Research Apprenticeship Program (URAP)
programs.summary: Undergraduates do a summer research apprenticeship in an Army-funded university lab under a faculty mentor.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents enrolled in college.
programs.format: In person, University labs across the US

programs.title: NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU)
programs.summary: A directory of hundreds of summer research sites at colleges and labs, funded by NSF. Undergraduates join a research group for about ten weeks.
body: Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents enrolled in college.
programs.when: Most sites close in February or March
programs.cost: Paid stipend, housing and travel often covered
programs.format: In person, Sites across the US and abroad

programs.title: Scripps Research Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF)
programs.summary: Undergraduates spend ten weeks doing research in a Scripps Research lab in chemistry, biology or neuroscience.

programs.title: SPS Summer Internship Program
programs.summary: Ten-week internships in physics research, education and policy at organizations in Washington, DC, with housing, a stipend and travel paid.
body: Who can apply: Undergraduate SPS members.

programs.title: Explore Microsoft
programs.summary: A 12-week paid summer internship in the US for first- and second-year college students. Interns build software development skills on real projects with a Microsoft team.
body: Who can apply: First- and second-year college students.
programs.format: In person, Microsoft offices, mainly Redmond, WA

programs.title: Jane Street Programs for First- and Second-Year Students
programs.summary: Short programs, including INSIGHT and a first-year trading and technology program, where early college students learn how the firm trades and writes software, in the office for a few days.
body: Who can apply: First- and second-year college students.
programs.when: Varies by program, often fall and winter
programs.format: In person, New York, London and Hong Kong

programs.title: Discover Citadel
programs.summary: A two-day program for college freshmen and sophomores to learn about investing and market making at Citadel and Citadel Securities.
body: Who can apply: College freshmen and sophomores.

programs.title: MITRE Co-ops and Internships
programs.summary: Paid internships and co-ops for college and graduate students on MITRE research and engineering projects for government agencies.
body: Who can apply: Most roles need US citizenship.
programs.when: Rolling, most summer roles post in fall
programs.format: Hybrid, MITRE sites across the US

programs.title: Amazon Student Internships
programs.summary: Paid summer internships at Amazon for college and graduate students in software, hardware, data science and other technical roles.
programs.when: Rolling, most roles post in late summer and fall
programs.format: In person, Amazon offices across the US

programs.title: Susquehanna (SIG) Campus Programs
programs.summary: Paid internships and co-ops in trading, quantitative research and software for college students, plus shorter programs for students earlier in college.
programs.format: In person, Bala Cynwyd, PA and other offices

programs.title: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
programs.summary: Scholarships of $100,000, $50,000 or $25,000 for students 18 or younger who have finished a significant piece of work in STEM, literature, music, philosophy, or a project outside those areas.
body: Applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents living in the US, and 18 or younger on the deadline. There is no minimum age.
programs.when: Applications open in the fall and are due in February
timeline: All applicants notified by this date

programs.title: Rise
programs.org: Schmidt Futures and the Rhodes Trust
programs.summary: A global program that picks teenagers who want to work on big problems. Winners get long-term support, including need-based college scholarships and project grants.
body: Award: Need-based college scholarship, project grants, funded summit.
Who can apply: Ages 15 to 17, any country.

programs.title: Non-Trivial Fellowship
programs.summary: An online research fellowship where teenagers turn an idea about a big problem into a research project, with guidance over about 8 weeks.
body: Award: $2,000 scholarship; top fellows can get up to $10,000.
Who can apply: High school students ages 14 to 20.

programs.title: Hack Club
programs.summary: A nonprofit network of teen-run coding clubs with free events, hackathons and hardware programs. Members build projects and can run teen-led nonprofits through its fiscal sponsorship tool, HCB.
body: Who can apply: Teens ages 13 to 18.

programs.title: NCWIT Aspirations in Computing High School Award
programs.org: National Center for Women & Information Technology
programs.summary: A yearly award that recognizes high school students for their interest and work in computing. Winners join a community that shares scholarships, internships and mentoring.
body: Award: Recognition and access to a network of opportunities.

programs.title: Udall Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for sophomores and juniors planning careers in the environment, or in Tribal public policy or Native health care. Your college nominates you first.
body: Award: Up to 65 scholarships of $7,500.
Who can apply: Sophomores and juniors nominated by their college.
programs.when: Usually early March (after a campus nomination)

programs.title: RISE Germany
programs.summary: Summer research internships in Germany for undergraduates. You are matched with a PhD student at a German university or institute and work in English.
body: Award: Monthly stipend for three months, housing help.
Who can apply: Undergraduates at North American, British and Irish universities.

programs.title: Google Summer of Code
programs.summary: A program where newcomers to open source write code for an open source organization with a mentor. You write a proposal, and if accepted you work on it remotely for 8 to 22 weeks.
body: Award: Stipend.
Who can apply: 18 or older, new to open source.
programs.when: Contributor applications usually March to April

programs.title: Outreachy
programs.summary: Paid, remote three-month internships on open source projects for people underrepresented in tech. You make small contributions during an application period, then work with a mentor.
body: Award: $7,000 stipend.
Who can apply: People who face underrepresentation or bias in tech in their country.
programs.when: Twice a year: usually early February and early August

programs.title: MLH Fellowship
programs.summary: A 12-week remote program where fellows work in small teams on software, site reliability or Web3 engineering projects with a mentor.
body: Award: Educational stipend.
programs.when: Rolling, several start dates a year

programs.title: SMART Scholarship-for-Service
programs.summary: Pays for a STEM degree and includes summer internships at a Defense lab or agency. After graduating you work for that agency for a set time.
body: Award: Tuition, stipend and summer internships, with a work commitment.
Who can apply: US citizens in STEM degree programs.

programs.title: Neo Scholars
programs.summary: A program run by the venture firm Neo for strong computer science undergraduates. Scholars get mentoring from founders and engineers and join a small peer group.
body: Who can apply: Undergraduates in computer science.

programs.title: Kleiner Perkins Fellows
programs.summary: Students work at a startup backed by the venture firm Kleiner Perkins, with mentoring, founder talks and workshops alongside the job.
body: Award: Paid role at a startup.
programs.when: Varies, roles post on the application portal

programs.title: Thiel Fellowship
programs.summary: A two-year grant for young people who leave school to build a company, a research project or another venture. Fellows also get mentoring and a network of founders.
body: Award: $250,000 over two years, no equity taken.
Who can apply: 22 or younger, no college degree; you leave school to accept.

programs.title: Emergent Ventures
programs.org: Mercatus Center at George Mason University
programs.summary: Grants and fellowships for people with ambitious ideas, including teenagers. You fill out a short online application about your project.
body: Award: Grants vary by project.
Who can apply: Age 13 and up, any country.

programs.title: Z Fellows
programs.summary: A one-week program that puts ten builders in a room with founders of large tech companies. Most sessions are online and the last day is in San Francisco or New York.
body: Award: Optional $10,000 investment.
Who can apply: No age limit; students and dropouts can apply.

programs.title: 1517 Medici Grants
programs.summary: Small, no-strings grants for students and dropouts working on their own projects. You email a short video about who you are and what the money would do.
body: Award: At least $1,000.
Who can apply: Based in North America; projects not for school credit.

programs.title: O'Shaughnessy Fellowship
programs.summary: A one-year grant for researchers, builders and creators working on an idea. Fellows keep full ownership of what they make.

programs.title: Dorm Room Fund
programs.summary: A student-run venture fund that invests in startups founded by students or recent graduates. Founders also get advisors and a network of other student founders.
body: Award: Early investment.
Who can apply: Current students and recent graduates.

programs.title: Activate Fellowship
programs.summary: A two-year fellowship for scientists turning hard science research into a company. Fellows work full time on the startup, in person at a hub or remotely.
body: Award: $100,000 in research funding, plus support.
Who can apply: Authorized to work in the US; full-time founder.
programs.when: Yearly; fellows are picked in spring and start July 1
programs.format: Hybrid, Berkeley, Boston, Houston, New York, or remote

programs.title: Nucleate Activator
programs.summary: An eight-month program that helps teams of researchers turn life science research into a startup, with weekly workshops and a demo day.
body: Who can apply: Research teams with approval from their lab head.

programs.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)
programs.summary: Three years of funding for research-based master's and PhD students in STEM. College seniors and early graduate students apply with a research plan and personal statement.
body: Award: $37,000 stipend and $16,000 education allowance per year, for 3 years.
Who can apply: US citizens, nationals and permanent residents; seniors and early grad students.

programs.title: NDSEG Fellowship
programs.summary: Pays for PhD study in science and engineering fields that matter to the Air Force, Army and Navy research offices.
body: Award: Tuition and stipend.
Who can apply: US citizens and nationals starting or early in a PhD.

programs.title: Hertz Fellowship
programs.summary: A PhD fellowship in applied science, engineering and math. Applicants go through a written application and two rounds of interviews.
body: Award: Up to five years of stipend and tuition.
Who can apply: College seniors and early PhD students.

programs.title: DOE Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (CSGF)
programs.org: US Department of Energy, run by the Krell Institute
programs.summary: Funding for PhD students who use high-performance computing in science and engineering. Fellows also spend at least 12 weeks at a DOE national lab.
body: Award: $45,000 yearly stipend plus tuition, up to four years.
Who can apply: US citizens and permanent residents; seniors and first-year grad students.

programs.title: DOE NNSA Stewardship Science Graduate Fellowship (SSGF)
programs.org: US Department of Energy, run by the Krell Institute
programs.summary: Funding for PhD students in areas such as high energy density physics, nuclear science and materials under extreme conditions, with a practicum at a national lab.
body: Award: Stipend and tuition.
Who can apply: US citizens.
programs.when: Usually the second Wednesday of January; opens late October

programs.title: DOE NNSA Laboratory Residency Graduate Fellowship (LRGF)
programs.org: US Department of Energy, run by the Krell Institute
programs.summary: Funding for PhD students in engineering, physics, materials, math or computational science, including two 12-week research stays at DOE labs.
body: Award: $45,000 yearly stipend plus tuition, up to four years.
Who can apply: US citizens with at least 18 months left in the PhD.

programs.title: DOE Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR)
programs.org: US Department of Energy Office of Science
programs.summary: Supports PhD students doing part of their thesis research at a DOE national lab for 3 to 12 months, working with a lab scientist.
body: Award: Supplemental funding for the lab stay.
Who can apply: US citizens and permanent residents in a PhD program.

programs.title: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
programs.summary: Full funding for graduate study in any Stanford program, plus a leadership program with other scholars. You apply both to Knight-Hennessy and to your Stanford program.
body: Award: Up to three years of tuition, living stipend and travel.

programs.title: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
programs.summary: Graduate school funding for immigrants and children of immigrants in any field, including science and engineering. About 30 fellows are chosen each year after interviews.
body: Award: Half of tuition and up to $25,000 a year in stipend, for two years.
Who can apply: 30 or younger; immigrant or child of immigrants.

programs.title: HHMI Gilliam Fellows Program
programs.summary: Supports PhD students in the biological and biomedical sciences together with their thesis advisers. Fellows can later apply for postdoc support.
body: Award: Up to three years of stipend support and an allowance.
Who can apply: Second- or third-year PhD students at eligible US schools.

programs.title: Rhodes Scholarship (United States)
programs.summary: Full funding for graduate study at the University of Oxford in any field, including science and engineering. Applicants go through state or district interviews.
body: Award: Full funding at Oxford; 32 US scholars a year.
Who can apply: US citizens finishing or recently finished college.

programs.title: Marshall Scholarship
programs.summary: Pays for graduate study at a UK university in any field. Many scholars study science, engineering or medicine.
body: Award: Tuition and living costs.
Who can apply: US citizens with a GPA of 3.7 or higher.
programs.when: Usually late September or early October

programs.title: Churchill Scholarship
programs.org: Winston Churchill Foundation of the United States
programs.summary: A year of graduate study or research in science, math or engineering at Churchill College, Cambridge. Students must be nominated by a participating US college.
body: Award: Full funding for a year at Cambridge; 18 scholars a year.
Who can apply: Nominated by one of about 134 participating institutions.
programs.when: Usually early November (campus deadlines are earlier)

programs.title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
programs.summary: Full-cost scholarships for graduate study at the University of Cambridge for students from outside the UK, in any subject.
body: Award: Full cost of study.
Who can apply: Citizens of any country outside the UK.
programs.when: October 14, 2026 (US citizens living in the US)

programs.title: Fulbright US Student Program
programs.summary: Grants for graduating seniors, graduate students and young professionals to study, do research or teach English abroad for about a year. Research projects in STEM are common.
body: Award: Travel and living costs abroad.
Who can apply: US citizens.

programs.title: GEM Fellowship
programs.summary: Funds master's and PhD study in engineering and applied science, paired with paid internships at partner employers.
body: Award: Graduate funding and paid internships.

programs.title: Google PhD Fellowship
programs.summary: Supports PhD students doing research in computer science and related areas. Students cannot apply directly; universities nominate them.
body: Award: In the US and Canada, up to $85,000 a year for two years.
Who can apply: Nominated by an eligible university.

programs.title: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship
programs.summary: Funding for PhD students in computer science and engineering working on topics close to NVIDIA's research. Fellows do a summer internship at NVIDIA.
body: Award: Up to $60,000.
Who can apply: PhD students who have finished their first year.

programs.title: Qualcomm Innovation Fellowship (North America)
programs.summary: PhD students propose a research idea, often as a team of two, in areas like AI, wireless and hardware. Winners get funding and Qualcomm mentors.
body: Award: Fellowship funding and mentoring.
Who can apply: PhD students at eligible schools in the US and Canada.

programs.title: Microsoft Research Fellowship
programs.summary: PhD students, postdocs and faculty propose research to do in collaboration with Microsoft Research. Funding goes to the school as a gift.
body: Award: $47,000 in the US and Canada.

programs.title: Apple Scholars in AI/ML PhD Fellowship
programs.summary: Two years of funding for PhD students in machine learning and AI, plus an Apple research mentor and internship chances. Universities nominate the students.
body: Award: Tuition and fees plus a stipend of up to $40,000 a year.
Who can apply: Nominated by an invited university.

programs.title: Jane Street Graduate Research Fellowship
programs.summary: A year of funding for PhD students in computer science, electrical engineering, math, physics or statistics.
body: Award: Full tuition and fees plus a $45,000 stipend.
Who can apply: PhD students with a year or more left, or starting a PhD in fall 2027.

programs.title: Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship
programs.summary: Funding for PhD students in machine learning, natural language processing and related areas. Fellows spend a paid summer internship at Bloomberg.
body: Award: Full tuition, $45,000 stipend and a paid summer internship.
programs.format: In person, New York, London or Toronto for the internship

programs.title: Siebel Scholars
programs.summary: An award for top graduate students in computer science, bioengineering, energy science and business at partner universities. Schools choose the scholars; there is no open application.
body: Award: $35,000 for the final year of study.

programs.title: Schmidt Science Fellows
programs.summary: A postdoc fellowship for new PhDs in science, engineering, math or computing who want to switch to a different field. You are nominated by your PhD school.
body: Award: Postdoc funding and a program of global meetings.
Who can apply: PhD finished between May 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027 at a partner school.

programs.title: AI2050 Fellows
programs.summary: Funds researchers working on hard problems in making AI good for society, including early-career researchers.
body: Award: Research funding.
Who can apply: Early-career and senior researchers.

programs.title: Cohere Labs Scholars Program
programs.summary: A paid, full-time, remote program where new researchers lead a machine learning research project with mentors. Research experience is not required.
body: Award: Paid position.
programs.when: Applications open in fall; the program starts in January

programs.title: MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars)
programs.summary: A 12-week, full-time research program on AI safety and alignment. Scholars work on a project with a mentor in Berkeley or London.
body: Award: Stipend, housing and travel.
programs.format: In person, Berkeley, California or London, UK

programs.title: Career Development and Transition Funding
programs.summary: Grants to individuals building careers in reducing global catastrophic risks, such as AI safety or biosecurity. It can pay for graduate study, unpaid internships or independent study.
body: Award: Varies by need.

programs.title: NIH Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Predoctoral Fellowship (F31)
programs.summary: Funds PhD and MD/PhD students in health-related research. You write a research and training plan with your adviser.
body: Award: Stipend, tuition and fees.
programs.when: Standard NIH fellowship dates: April 8, August 8, December 8

programs.title: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
programs.summary: A national scholarship for high school seniors who show leadership and service. 150 students are picked each year after an online application, essays and interviews.
body: Who can apply: US high school seniors.

programs.title: QuestBridge National College Match
programs.summary: Low-income seniors apply once and rank partner colleges. Students who match get a full four-year scholarship covering tuition, room and board.
body: Award: Full four-year scholarship at a partner college.
Who can apply: High-achieving seniors from low-income families.

programs.title: Jack Kent Cooke College Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for high-achieving seniors with financial need. It pays a large share of college costs each year, plus advising.
body: Award: Up to $55,000 per year.
Who can apply: US seniors with financial need, family income up to about $95,000.

programs.title: The Gates Scholarship
programs.summary: A last-dollar scholarship for Pell-eligible minority seniors. It covers the full cost of attendance not paid by other aid.
body: Award: Full cost of attendance.
Who can apply: Pell-eligible African American, American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian and Pacific Islander American, or Hispanic American seniors.

programs.title: Dell Scholars Program
programs.summary: A scholarship for students in a college readiness program who have financial need. Winners also get a laptop, textbook credits and support through college.
body: Award: $20,000 plus laptop and support.
Who can apply: Pell-eligible seniors in an approved college readiness program.

programs.title: Elks Most Valuable Student
programs.summary: A scholarship for seniors judged on scholarship, leadership and financial need. Local Elks lodges judge first, then state and national rounds.
body: Award: $1,000 to $50,000 over four years.
Who can apply: US citizen high school seniors.

programs.title: Burger King Scholars
programs.summary: Scholarships for high school seniors and Burger King employees based on grades, work, service and need.
body: Who can apply: Seniors and students in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico.
programs.when: October 15 to December 15, 2026, or until 30,000 applications

programs.title: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for students who have faced hard circumstances and have financial need. Winners also attend a conference in Washington, DC.
body: Who can apply: US juniors applying for the senior year, family income up to about $65,000.

programs.title: National Merit Scholarship Program
programs.summary: Students enter by taking the PSAT/NMSQT as juniors. High scorers become Semifinalists, apply as seniors, and Finalists compete for $2,500 awards and corporate or college scholarships.
body: Award: $2,500 and corporate or college scholarships.
Who can apply: US high school juniors who take the PSAT/NMSQT.
programs.when: PSAT in October of junior year

programs.title: Ron Brown Scholar Program
programs.summary: A scholarship and mentoring program for Black high school seniors who show academic promise, leadership and service.
body: Award: $40,000 over four years.
Who can apply: Black/African American US citizen or permanent resident seniors.

programs.title: Cameron Impact Scholarship
programs.summary: A full-tuition scholarship for seniors with strong grades, leadership and service. Finalists interview.
body: Award: Full tuition for four years.
Who can apply: US citizen or permanent resident seniors with a 3.7 GPA or above.

programs.title: Hagan Scholarship
programs.summary: A renewable scholarship for students from rural areas with financial need. It also pays for summer work and study abroad.
body: Award: Up to $48,000 over four years.
Who can apply: Seniors from rural or small-town public schools with need.

programs.title: Barry Goldwater Scholarship
programs.org: Barry Goldwater Scholarship and Excellence in Education Foundation
programs.summary: A national award for college sophomores and juniors who plan research careers in natural science, math or engineering. Students apply through their college, which nominates up to four.
body: Award: Up to $7,500 per year.
Who can apply: US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, nominated by their college.

programs.title: Astronaut Scholarship
programs.summary: Scholarships for STEM juniors and seniors at partner universities who have done research. Faculty nominate students, and winners meet astronauts and attend a conference.
body: Award: Up to $15,000.
Who can apply: US citizens at partner universities, nominated by faculty.
programs.when: Nomination by partner university, usually spring

programs.title: DoD SMART Scholarship
programs.summary: Pays full tuition and a stipend for STEM degrees, plus paid summer internships at a defense lab. After graduation you work for the Department of Defense for the same number of years you were funded.
body: Award: Full tuition, yearly stipend, paid internships and a job.
Who can apply: US citizens 18 or older with at least one year of study left.

programs.title: NOAA Ernest F. Hollings Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: Pays for two years of study for college sophomores in ocean, weather, climate or related sciences. It includes a paid 10-week summer internship at a NOAA site.
body: Award: Up to $9,500 per year plus a paid summer internship.
Who can apply: US citizen college sophomores with a 3.0 GPA.

programs.title: NOAA Educational Partnership Program Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: Scholarships for sophomores at minority serving institutions studying NOAA-related sciences. It includes two paid summer internships at NOAA.
body: Award: Up to $9,500 per year plus paid internships.
Who can apply: US citizen sophomores at minority serving institutions.

programs.title: CyberCorps Scholarship for Service
programs.org: National Science Foundation and US Office of Personnel Management
programs.summary: Pays tuition and a stipend for students studying cybersecurity at a participating college. In return you work in a government cybersecurity job for as long as you were funded.
body: Award: Tuition, stipend of $27,000 (undergrad) or $37,000 (grad) per year.
Who can apply: US citizens at a participating college.

programs.title: NIH Undergraduate Scholarship Program
programs.summary: Scholarships for students from low-income families committed to biomedical research careers. Winners do paid summer research at NIH and work there after graduating.
body: Award: Up to $20,000 per year.
Who can apply: US citizens or permanent residents from low-income families.

programs.title: Army ROTC Scholarship
programs.summary: Pays college tuition for students who join Army ROTC and serve as officers after graduating. High school seniors apply for four-year awards.
body: Award: Full tuition or room and board, plus stipend.
Who can apply: US citizens who agree to serve.

programs.title: Navy ROTC Scholarship
programs.summary: Pays tuition and gives a stipend to students who join Navy or Marine Corps ROTC. The Navy option favors engineering and technical majors.
body: Award: Full tuition, fees and monthly stipend.
Who can apply: US citizens 17 to 23 who agree to serve.

programs.title: Air Force ROTC Scholarship
programs.summary: Scholarships for students who join Air Force or Space Force ROTC. Most high school awards go to technical majors like engineering and computer science.
body: Award: Full or partial tuition plus stipend.
Who can apply: US citizens who agree to serve.

programs.title: DOE Scholars Program
programs.summary: Paid summer or year-long internships at Department of Energy sites and offices for college and graduate students in STEM and policy.
body: Award: Paid stipend and travel.
Who can apply: US citizens 18 or older.

programs.title: DOE University Nuclear Leadership Program Scholarship
programs.org: US Department of Energy, Office of Nuclear Energy
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduates in nuclear engineering and related fields such as health physics, radiochemistry and nuclear materials. Students apply online.
body: Award: $10,000 at 4-year schools, $5,000 at 2-year schools.
Who can apply: Students in a nuclear-related major at a US college.

programs.title: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for high school seniors from underserved communities who plan to study computer science. It covers unmet financial need and comes with a paid summer internship at Amazon.
body: Award: Up to $10,000 per year for four years, plus a paid Amazon internship.
Who can apply: US seniors planning a computer science degree, with financial need.
programs.when: Usually opens in fall, closes in January (2025-26 cycle closed)

programs.title: AFCEA STEM Major Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for college students in STEM majors, with a separate award for cybersecurity. One application puts you in the running for all of them.
body: Award: $2,500 (STEM Major), $5,000 (Cyber Security).
Who can apply: US citizens in STEM degree programs.

programs.title: Center for Cyber Safety and Education Scholarships
programs.org: ISC2 Center for Cyber Safety and Education
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduate and graduate students studying cybersecurity, including awards for women.
body: Who can apply: Students in a cybersecurity or related program.

programs.title: NSA Stokes Educational Scholarship Program
programs.summary: Pays college tuition for students in fields like computer science and computer engineering. You work at NSA each summer and then work there after graduating.
body: Award: Tuition, yearly salary and summer work at NSA.
Who can apply: US citizen seniors and early college students with a strong GPA.

programs.title: CIA Stokes Scholarship Program
programs.summary: A need-based scholarship that pays college tuition. Students intern at the CIA in summers and work there after graduating.
body: Award: Tuition assistance and paid summer work.
Who can apply: US citizens with financial need.
programs.when: Check the CIA student programs page

programs.title: Science Ambassador Scholarship
programs.summary: Women and non-binary students film a three-minute video teaching a STEM topic. Five winners get money for undergraduate STEM tuition.
body: Award: $20,000 (five winners).
Who can apply: Women and non-binary high school seniors and undergraduates in STEM.

programs.title: NCWIT Award for Aspirations in Computing
programs.org: National Center for Women & Information Technology
programs.summary: Recognizes high school students of marginalized genders for work and interest in computing. Winners join a large community with scholarship and internship leads.
body: Award: Recognition, prizes and access to scholarships.
Who can apply: US high school students who are women, genderqueer or non-binary.

programs.title: ASME Scholarships
programs.summary: One application puts ASME student members in the running for many scholarships in mechanical engineering and related fields. Some awards are for high school seniors.
body: Who can apply: ASME student members; some awards open to seniors.
programs.cost: Free (ASME student membership for most awards)

programs.title: IEEE PES Scholarship Plus Initiative
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduate electrical engineering students interested in power and energy. Winners can renew and get help finding internships.
body: Who can apply: Undergraduate EE students in the US and Canada.

programs.title: AIChE Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduate chemical engineering students who are AIChE members, including awards for students in their first years.
body: Who can apply: AIChE undergraduate student members.

programs.title: ACS Scholars Program
programs.summary: A renewable scholarship for undergraduates studying chemistry and related fields, with mentoring from ACS members.
body: Who can apply: US students planning degrees in chemistry-related fields, with financial need.

programs.title: AMS Undergraduate Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduates in meteorology, ocean and atmospheric science, and for seniors starting college in these fields.
body: Who can apply: Students planning careers in atmospheric and related sciences.

programs.title: SPIE Optics and Photonics Education Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for students studying optics, photonics and related fields. Students must be SPIE student members.
body: Who can apply: SPIE student members.

programs.title: AWG Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for women studying geology, earth science and related fields, from undergraduates through graduate school.
body: Who can apply: Women in geoscience programs.

programs.title: AIAA Foundation Scholarships
programs.org: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduate AIAA student members studying aerospace and related engineering fields.
body: Who can apply: AIAA undergraduate student members.

programs.title: ANS Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for incoming freshmen, undergraduates and graduate students in nuclear science and engineering. Winners must join ANS before funds are paid.
body: Who can apply: Students in nuclear-related programs.

programs.title: ASHRAE Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for students studying heating, cooling, building systems and related engineering, plus travel grants to the ASHRAE conference.
body: Who can apply: Undergraduates in HVAC-related engineering programs.

programs.title: SAE International Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for high school seniors and college students heading into mobility engineering such as automotive and aerospace.
body: Who can apply: Seniors and undergraduates planning engineering degrees.

programs.title: SWE Scholarships
programs.summary: One application puts you in the running for many SWE scholarships for engineering and computer science students. Incoming freshmen, undergraduates and graduate students can apply.
body: Award: Varies by scholarship.
Who can apply: Students planning ABET-accredited engineering, technology or CS degrees.
programs.when: Usually open December to February (freshmen) and spring (upperclass)

programs.title: AWIS Undergraduate Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for women undergraduates in science fields, including an award for first-generation college students.
body: Who can apply: Women college students, freshman through junior year.

programs.title: ScholarSHPE
programs.summary: Scholarships for SHPE members studying STEM, from high school seniors through graduate students.
body: Who can apply: SHPE members.

programs.title: NSBE Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for NSBE members, from high school seniors to graduate students in engineering and technical fields.
body: Who can apply: NSBE members.

programs.title: AISES Scholarships
programs.org: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
programs.summary: Scholarships for American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian students studying STEM, including the A.T. Anderson Scholarship.
body: Who can apply: Indigenous students who are AISES members, GPA 3.0 or higher.

programs.title: HSF Scholar Program
programs.summary: Merit scholarships for students of Hispanic heritage, with extra support for STEM majors. Scholars also get career services and a conference.
body: Who can apply: Students of Hispanic heritage with a 3.0 GPA.
programs.when: Usually opens January, closes mid February

programs.title: UNCF Scholarships
programs.summary: UNCF runs hundreds of scholarships, including many for STEM majors, mostly for students at HBCUs and other colleges.
body: Who can apply: Varies by scholarship.

programs.title: APIA Scholars
programs.org: Asian & Pacific Islander American Scholarship Fund
programs.summary: Scholarships for Asian American and Pacific Islander students with financial need, many of them first-generation college students.
body: Who can apply: AANHPI students in the US and territories.

programs.title: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
programs.summary: Scholarships, mentoring and leadership training for LGBTQ+ college and graduate students.
body: Award: Up to $15,000.
Who can apply: LGBTQ+ students at US colleges.

programs.title: Out to Innovate Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for LGBTQ+ undergraduate and graduate students in STEM fields.
body: Who can apply: LGBTQ+ STEM students.

programs.title: Udall Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: For college sophomores and juniors committed to careers in the environment, or Native American students in tribal policy or health care. Students are nominated by their college.
body: Award: $7,500 (up to 65 awards).
Who can apply: US sophomores and juniors nominated by their college.

programs.title: Churchill Scholarship
programs.org: Winston Churchill Foundation of the United States
programs.summary: Funds a year of graduate study in science, math or engineering at the University of Cambridge. College seniors are nominated by partner universities.
body: Award: Full tuition, living costs and travel for a year at Cambridge.
Who can apply: US citizen seniors or recent graduates at partner universities.
programs.format: In person, University of Cambridge, UK

programs.title: Lockheed Martin STEM Scholarship
programs.summary: A renewable scholarship for high school seniors and college students with financial need who study engineering or computer science.
body: Who can apply: US students with financial need in engineering or CS.

programs.title: Tau Beta Pi Scholarships
programs.org: Tau Beta Pi, the Engineering Honor Society
programs.summary: Scholarships for Tau Beta Pi members in their senior year of engineering study.
body: Who can apply: Tau Beta Pi members.

programs.title: NASA Space Grant Scholarships
programs.org: NASA National Space Grant College and Fellowship Project
programs.summary: Each state has a Space Grant consortium that gives scholarships and internships to college students in STEM. You apply through your state consortium.
body: Who can apply: US citizens at consortium member colleges.

programs.title: Taco Bell Live Más Scholarship
programs.summary: Students send a short video about a passion they are pursuing, which can be STEM. No grades or test scores are required.
body: Award: Up to $25,000.
Who can apply: US students 16 to 26.

programs.title: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
programs.summary: A renewable scholarship for high school seniors who show determination and plan to make an impact. Winners also get financial workshops.
body: Award: $5,000 per year for up to four years.
Who can apply: US high school seniors.

programs.title: Jack Kent Cooke Undergraduate Transfer Scholarship
programs.summary: For community college students with financial need who are transferring to a four-year college.
body: Award: Up to $55,000 per year.
Who can apply: Community college students with a 3.5 GPA and financial need.

programs.title: Posse STEM Program
programs.summary: High schools and community groups nominate students, who go through group interviews. Winners attend a partner college in a team of about ten STEM students with full-tuition leadership scholarships.
body: Award: Full tuition at a partner college.
Who can apply: Seniors in Posse cities, nominated by their school or a community group.
programs.when: Nominations in spring and summer before senior year

programs.title: Coolidge Scholarship
programs.summary: A full-ride merit scholarship for high school juniors, usable at any accredited US college. Students apply with essays and grades, and finalists interview.
body: Award: Full tuition, room, board and expenses for four years.
Who can apply: US high school juniors.

programs.title: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
programs.org: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and GE Aerospace
programs.summary: A scholarship for high school seniors who show leadership, drive, integrity and citizenship.
body: Award: Up to $40,000.
Who can apply: US high school seniors.

programs.title: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
programs.summary: One application covers more than 60 scholarships for students studying manufacturing engineering and technology, from high school seniors to graduate students.
body: Who can apply: Students planning manufacturing or related degrees.

programs.title: AIST Foundation Scholarships
programs.org: Association for Iron & Steel Technology Foundation
programs.summary: Scholarships and paid internships for engineering students interested in the steel industry.
body: Who can apply: Undergraduate engineering and science students.

programs.title: American Indian College Fund Scholarships
programs.summary: One yearly application for many scholarships for American Indian and Alaska Native students at tribal colleges and other colleges.
body: Award: Varies, most $2,000 to $3,000.
Who can apply: Enrolled members or descendants of a federally or state recognized tribe.

programs.title: Cobell Scholarship
programs.summary: Scholarships for enrolled tribal members attending college, graduate school or vocational programs.
body: Who can apply: Enrolled members of a federally recognized tribe.

programs.title: Thurgood Marshall College Fund Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships, many funded by companies and aimed at STEM majors, for students at public HBCUs and other member schools.
body: Who can apply: Students at TMCF member schools.

programs.title: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
programs.summary: A four-year scholarship with mentoring and a leadership program for students of color with financial need.
body: Who can apply: High school seniors of color with financial need.

programs.title: USDA 1890 National Scholars Program
