programs.summary: Pays full tuition, fees, books, and room and board for students in agriculture, food science, natural resources and related majors at 1890 land-grant universities. Scholars do paid USDA summer internships and then work for USDA.
body: Award: Full tuition, fees, books, room and board, plus paid internships.
Who can apply: US citizens with a 3.0 GPA attending or accepted to an 1890 land-grant university.

programs.title: DoD Cyber Service Academy Scholarship
programs.summary: Pays for college study in cybersecurity and related fields at partner schools. Recipients work for the Department of Defense after graduating.
body: Award: Tuition, fees, books and a stipend.
Who can apply: US citizens at designated partner colleges.

programs.title: Dr. Robert H. Goddard Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for a US student planning a STEM career, with preference for space-related interests. The winner also speaks at the Goddard Memorial Dinner.
body: Who can apply: US citizen high school seniors through undergraduates.

programs.title: SASE Scholarships
programs.org: Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers
programs.summary: Scholarships for SASE members who show excellence in STEM. The number and size of awards changes each year.
body: Who can apply: SASE collegiate and professional members.

programs.title: Stamps Scholars Program
programs.summary: Merit scholarships given through about 40 partner colleges. Students are considered when they apply to a partner school, and some schools require a separate application.
body: Award: Up to full cost of attendance plus enrichment funds, varies by college.
Who can apply: Seniors applying to a partner college.
programs.when: Set by each partner college, often with early admission deadlines

programs.title: NHS Scholarship
programs.org: National Association of Secondary School Principals
programs.summary: Scholarships for National Honor Society members who are seniors. Each chapter can nominate students, who then apply online.
body: Who can apply: Senior NHS members nominated by their chapter.

programs.title: P.E.O. STAR Scholarship
programs.summary: A scholarship for young women who are high school seniors, sponsored by a local P.E.O. chapter.
body: Who can apply: Women high school seniors in the US or Canada, sponsored by a P.E.O. chapter.
programs.when: Usually fall, through a local chapter

programs.title: SEG Foundation Scholarships
programs.summary: Scholarships for undergraduate and graduate students planning careers in applied geophysics.
body: Who can apply: Students planning geophysics or related degrees.

programs.title: Hack Club high school hackathon list
programs.summary: A list of hackathons run by and for high schoolers around the world. Filter by place or online and sign up for one near you.
body: Who can apply: Mostly high school students.

programs.title: Hack Club programs
programs.summary: Hack Club's list of current programs and events for teens. Most follow a build-and-ship model: you finish a project and Hack Club sends you hardware, grants or a trip.
body: Who can apply: Teens, 18 and under.

programs.title: Hack Club events calendar
programs.summary: Online AMAs, live coding sessions, CTFs and talks for teens in the Hack Club community.
body: Who can apply: Teens.

programs.title: MLH hackathon season
programs.summary: Schedule of hundreds of student hackathons each season, including some marked for high school students. Member events do not charge entry fees.
body: Who can apply: Varies by event; some are high school only.
programs.when: Rolling, season runs July 2026 to June 2027

programs.title: hackPHS
programs.summary: A high school hackathon in Princeton, New Jersey, listed in the MLH season. Teams build a project over a weekend.
body: Who can apply: High school students.

programs.title: HackMIT
programs.summary: A weekend hackathon at MIT where students build software and hardware projects in teams.
body: Who can apply: College students; check site for rules.
programs.when: Usually applications in summer, event in September

programs.title: TreeHacks
programs.summary: A 36-hour hackathon at Stanford. Admitted hackers get food, swag and travel help with regional caps.
body: Who can apply: Enrolled college students (undergrad or grad).

programs.title: PennApps
programs.summary: A long-running college hackathon at Penn. The next one is in the spring semester and applications open in October.
programs.when: Applications open October; event in spring

programs.title: HackTX
programs.summary: A student hackathon at the University of Texas at Austin that brings together over a thousand students each fall.

programs.title: Hack the North
programs.summary: Canada's largest hackathon, held each September at the University of Waterloo.
body: Who can apply: Mainly university students; check site for age rules.

programs.title: Cal Hacks
programs.summary: A 36-hour hackathon for college students, held in San Francisco. Teams of up to four build projects and compete for prizes.
body: Who can apply: College students and recent grads; high school students not eligible.
programs.when: Usually September deadlines; event in October

programs.title: HackGT
programs.summary: Georgia Tech's student hackathon, held each fall in Atlanta.

programs.title: MHacks
programs.summary: A 24-hour hackathon at the University of Michigan for students across North America.
programs.when: Usually September deadlines; event in fall

programs.title: HackPrinceton
programs.summary: A student hackathon at Princeton University held in the fall and spring.

programs.title: HackIllinois
programs.summary: A student hackathon at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign with a focus on building open source projects.

programs.title: LA Hacks
programs.summary: A spring hackathon at UCLA where college students build projects in teams.

programs.title: HackHarvard
programs.summary: A student hackathon at Harvard held each fall.

programs.title: HackDavis
programs.summary: A hackathon at UC Davis where students build projects that help society.

programs.title: HackRice
programs.summary: A student hackathon at Rice University in Houston.

programs.title: Bitcamp
programs.summary: A hackathon at the University of Maryland with beginner tracks and workshops.

programs.title: HackUMass
programs.summary: A hackathon at UMass Amherst with software and hardware tracks.

programs.title: Hack the 6ix
programs.summary: A student hackathon in Toronto held in the summer.

programs.title: Grace Hopper Celebration
programs.summary: A large conference for women and nonbinary people in computing, with talks, workshops and a big career fair.

programs.title: SWE Annual Conference (WE26)
programs.summary: SWE's yearly conference with sessions, a career fair and events for collegiate members. It can be attended in person or virtually.

programs.title: NSBE Annual Convention
programs.summary: NSBE's yearly convention with a career fair, workshops and pre-college (NSBE Jr.) programming and competitions.

programs.title: SHPE National Convention
